chapters.title: HTTP methods, status codes and data formats

topics.title: HTTP methods and idempotency (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE)
paraphrases: Which HTTP method creates, reads, replaces or partially updates a resource, and which methods are idempotent.

concepts.learning_objective: Which HTTP method creates, reads, replaces or partially updates a resource, and which methods are idempotent.

topics.title: HTTP status codes (2xx, 4xx, 5xx)
paraphrases: What common HTTP response codes such as 201, 403, 404 and 500 mean for an API client.

concepts.learning_objective: What common HTTP response codes such as 201, 403, 404 and 500 mean for an API client.

topics.title: JSON data types and the Content-Type header
paraphrases: How JSON represents arrays, booleans and other values, and how the Content-Type header declares the format of a request body.

concepts.learning_objective: How JSON represents arrays, booleans and other values, and how the Content-Type header declares the format of a request body.

topics.title: REST constraints: statelessness and uniform interface
paraphrases: The architectural constraints that make an API RESTful, especially stateless requests and a uniform interface to resources.

concepts.learning_objective: The architectural constraints that make an API RESTful, especially stateless requests and a uniform interface to resources.

topics.title: API pagination (limit, offset, cursor and Link header)
paraphrases: How APIs split large result sets into pages using limit, offset or cursors and point to the next and previous pages.

concepts.learning_objective: How APIs split large result sets into pages using limit, offset or cursors and point to the next and previous pages.

topics.title: API rate limiting, 429 and Retry-After
paraphrases: How APIs limit request rates with algorithms like token bucket and tell clients when to retry after a 429 response.

concepts.learning_objective: How APIs limit request rates with algorithms like token bucket and tell clients when to retry after a 429 response.

topics.title: API authentication methods: Basic Auth, API keys and bearer tokens
paraphrases: How clients prove identity to an API with Basic Auth, API keys sent in headers, or bearer tokens.

concepts.learning_objective: How clients prove identity to an API with Basic Auth, API keys sent in headers, or bearer tokens.

topics.title: OAuth 2.0 delegated authorization
paraphrases: What OAuth 2.0 is for: letting third-party applications access user data without sharing the user's credentials.

concepts.learning_objective: What OAuth 2.0 is for: letting third-party applications access user data without sharing the user's credentials.

topics.title: Sending API requests with curl
paraphrases: Using curl options to send request bodies, headers and methods when calling an API from the command line.

concepts.learning_objective: Using curl options to send request bodies, headers and methods when calling an API from the command line.

topics.title: Postman environments and variables
paraphrases: Using Postman environments to switch between sets of variables when testing APIs in different contexts.

concepts.learning_objective: Using Postman environments to switch between sets of variables when testing APIs in different contexts.
